summary: In Greek mythology, Alcyone (Ancient Greek Ἀλκυόνη) is a name borne by several women. The atlas node alcyone-sthenelid is the Perseid princess of Mycenae — daughter of Sthenelus son of Perseus and of Nicippe daughter of Pelops, sister of Eurystheus and of Medusa — distinct from the Aeolid wife of Ceyx and from the Pleiad of the same name.

sections.heading: Daughter of Sthenelus
paragraphs: Apollodorus places Alcyone among the children of Sthenelus and Nicippe (also called Antibia or Archippe in rival notices). She belongs to the Perseid generation that holds Mycenae before the birth-contest that crowns her brother Eurystheus over Heracles.

One tradition records that Heracles killed the centaur Homados after the creature attempted to rape her — a brief heroic debt owed by the princess to the hero her brother's house oppressed. Homonym care: not Alcyone wife of Ceyx (alcyone), not the Pleiad Alcyone, and not Cleopatra/Alcyone wife of Meleager.
